questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a feedback controller in a control system?

choices.B: To maintain stability and desired performance
choices.C: To reduce the system's response time
choices.D: To eliminate the need for human intervention

questions.solution: A feedback controller is used to maintain stability and desired performance by adjusting the system's inputs based on output measurements, ensuring it behaves as intended.
questions.explanation: Stability and desired performance are key aspects of control system design. Controllers help achieve these goals by comparing the actual output with the reference input and making necessary adjustments.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or D could indicate a misunderstanding of the controller's role; it doesn't increase variability or replace human intervention entirely.

questions.stem: In a control system, what does a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller primarily control?
questions.solution: A PID controller primarily controls setpoint tracking accuracy, ensuring the system output closely follows the desired reference input.
questions.explanation: PID controllers adjust inputs based on error (proportional term), past errors (integral term), and rate of change of error (derivative term). This combination helps achieve accurate setpoint tracking.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or C could result from confusion with other control system parameters; PID doesn't directly affect bandwidth or input signal amplitude.

questions.stem: What is the role of a lead compensator in control system design?

choices.A: To increase overshoot and settling time
choices.B: To improve stability by reducing phase lag
choices.C: To reduce steady-state error without affecting rise time

questions.solution: A lead compensator is used to improve stability in control systems by reducing phase lag, which helps prevent instability caused by excessive delay.
questions.explanation: Lead compensators introduce a controlled amount of phase lead at higher frequencies, counteracting the inherent phase lag in the system and improving its stability margins.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or D could result from misunderstanding compensator effects; they don't increase overshoot or handle input noise.

questions.stem: In a control system, what is the primary function of a PI controller when compared to a P-only controller?

choices.A: It eliminates steady-state error but increases settling time
choices.B: It improves rise time and overshoot
choices.C: It reduces steady-state error without affecting rise time
choices.D: It maintains the same performance as a P-only controller

questions.solution: A PI controller, compared to a P-only controller, reduces steady-state error by incorporating an integral term that accounts for past errors.
questions.explanation: The integral term in a PI controller helps eliminate steady-state error, which is not possible with a P-only (proportional) controller.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or B could result from confusion about the role of an integral term; it doesn't affect rise time or increase overshoot.

questions.stem: Which type of control system is best suited for systems with slow dynamics and a need for precise tracking?
questions.solution: A PID control system is well-suited for systems with slow dynamics and the requirement of precise tracking, as it combines proportional, integral, and derivative actions to achieve accurate control.
questions.explanation: PID controllers are designed to handle systems with varying dynamics and can provide good performance in terms of setpoint tracking accuracy.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or B could result from not understanding the need for feedback in systems requiring precise tracking; open-loop and on-off controls don't offer this.

questions.stem: In a control system, what is the primary advantage of using feedforward control?

choices.A: Reducing steady-state error due to constant disturbances
choices.B: Improving system stability by reducing phase lag
choices.C: Increasing the bandwidth of the system
choices.D: Minimizing the effect of unmodeled dynamics

questions.solution: The primary advantage of feedforward control is that it reduces steady-state error caused by constant disturbances, without affecting other performance metrics like rise time or overshoot.
questions.explanation: Feedforward control uses a copy of the disturbance signal to create a compensation signal, which helps抵消 the effect of the disturbance on the system output.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B or C could result from confusion with other control techniques; feedforward doesn't directly affect stability or bandwidth.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between a unity feedback control system and an open-loop control system?

choices.A: Unity feedback systems have no input/output relationship, while open-loop systems do.
choices.B: Open-loop systems have no feedback, while unity feedback systems have perfect feedback.
choices.C: Unity feedback systems are always stable, while open-loop systems can be unstable.
choices.D: Open-loop systems require manual adjustments, while unity feedback systems are automatic.

questions.solution: The main difference between a unity feedback control system and an open-loop system is that the former has perfect feedback, whereas the latter has no feedback at all.
questions.explanation: In a unity feedback system, the output is fed back to the input with a gain of 1, forming a closed loop. In contrast, an open-loop system operates without any feedback from the output.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or C could result from misconceptions about control system behavior; both types can have input/output relationships and stability depends on design.
